bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar's flood risk is changing, not just repeating | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: October 03, 2026 Bihar’s flood risk is changing, not just repeating Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Eklavya Prasad Bihar’s flood story is both familiar and evolving. While many communities face recurring inundation, erosion and infrastructure damage, changing flood patterns are pushing the geography of risk into new settlements, exposing more households to river floods, embankment breaches, flash floods and prolonged waterlogging Every year, Bihar counts its floods. Districts affected. Gram Panchayats affected. People evacuated. Relief camps, boats, damaged houses, families receiving gratuitous relief. These numbers matter; they let the state mobilise quickly. But after three consecutive years of flood figures, a harder question is becoming difficult to avoid: what does Bihar learn from one flood before the next arrives? The Disaster Management Department’s reports offer a starting point. On October 15, 2024, it recorded 28 affected districts, 979 Gram Panchayats and 52.46 lakh people. On October 15, 2025, the figures stood at 23 districts, 600 Gram Panchayats and 48 lakh people. The September 24, 2026 report shows 15 districts, 576 Gram Panchayats and 50.49 lakh people, a total likely to rise after the recent flooding along the Gandak. These are snapshots from different stages of different floods, so they do not measure severity. Yet the pattern is striking. The reported geography of impact has shifted considerably, while the number of people affected stays in a similar range. What changed because of what Bihar experienced the year before? Vulnerability in Bihar is neither wholly repetitive nor wholly new. Some embankments, settlements, roads and households face recurring exposure and accumulating loss. Elsewhere, a river shifts course, a breach redirects water, or a flash flood reaches people never considered at high risk. A single breach is an event; repeated breaches near the same spot signal persistent vulnerability, demanding a different response from a newly affected area. And when a flood behaves unexpectedly, that should reshape the state’s understanding of risk. Every flood produces information. Breaches are reported, roads cut, crops lost. Engineers inspect embankments; communities know where water entered and where it stagnated. When the water recedes, what happens to all this knowledge? Does a repeatedly flooded location acquire a risk profile? Does a newly affected area prompt a revision of vulnerability maps? Does a known breach or drainage failure shape how infrastructure is designed and maintained before the next monsoon? Bihar’s machinery for emergency response is extensive. What is harder to see is a learning loop connecting one year’s experience to the next year’s decisions. A response system asks: what must we do now? A learning system asks: why did this happen here, what did we learn, what must change, and who will make sure it does before it happens again? The first is indispensable during a flood. The second decides whether the state can move from recurring emergency management towards sustained risk reduction. Once the emergency passes, the questions should change. Why did the breach occur? national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today spoke with Captain Smit Machchhar over the phone, praising his bravery and presence of mind in foiling an alleged attempt to crash an Israel-bound flydubai flight. The Prime Minister said, Indians are not those who take lives, but those who are willing to risk their own lives to save others. He lauded Captain Machchhar for taking a split-second decision that helped save the lives of hundreds of passengers. On Wednesday, Captain Machchhar got seriously injured after being stabbed by his co-pilot in the cockpit of Flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The flight was carrying 174 passengers, including 27 children. The pilot is currently undergoing treatment at a hospital in the UAE. Speaking to the Prime Minister from his hospital bed, Captain Machchhar said his 17 years of flying experience, including 11 years as a captain, helped him understand the gravity of the situation and act immediately. He told the Prime Minister that he is away from the country but not from its culture. Prime Minister Modi said, special prayers were being offered across India for the pilot’s speedy recovery and thanked the governments of Saudi Arabia and the UAE for ensuring his treatment. The Prime Minister also said Captain Machchhar had enhanced the prestige of the Indian piloting community. Referring to Gandhi Jayanti being observed today, Mr Modi said the pilot had shown the world the true meaning of Ahimsa (non-violence). Captain Machchhar, who hails from Gujarat, expressed gratitude to the Prime Minister for the call and said he was receiving the best possible treatment. Mr Modi also spoke to him briefly in Gujarati.

national_raw_news.title: INS Trishul arrives in Spain after Varuna exercise with French Navy as part ongoing deployment
national_raw_news.content: INS Trishul arrives in Spain after Varuna exercise with French Navy as part ongoing deployment Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर INS Trishul arrives in Spain after Varuna exercise with French Navy as part ongoing deployment ANI | Updated: Oct 03, 2026 06:45 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Valencia [ Spain ], October 3 (ANI): Indian Naval Ship (INS) Trishul, a frontline guided-missile stealth frigate of the Indian Navy, arrived at Valencia , Spain , as part of its ongoing deployment to the Mediterranean, Atlantic and adjoining maritime regions, the Ministry of Defence said on Friday. According to the ministry, the frigate arrived at Valencia on September 30, during which it will undertake professional interactions, cross-deck visits, sporting events and cultural engagements with the Spanish Navy. The engagements are aimed at facilitating the exchange of operational experiences and fostering greater mutual understanding between the two navies. The visit is part of the Indian Navy's sustained maritime engagement with friendly foreign countries and partner navies, aimed at strengthening professional ties and enhancing cooperation at sea. The deployment comes after INS Trishul participated in the 24th edition of Exercise Varuna, the annual bilateral maritime exercise between the Indian Navy and the French Navy, at Toulon, France. INS Trishul had arrived at Toulon on September 22 to participate in the exercise. The harbour phase included professional, sporting and cultural engagements between personnel of the two navies. During the Toulon visit, the Commanding Officer of INS Trishul called on Rear Admiral Mackara Ouk, Deputy Commander-in-Chief for Operations (CECMED), and interacted with senior leadership of the French Navy. The Commanding Officer, officers and crew of INS Trishul also laid a wreath at the Mazargues War Memorial in Marseille in remembrance of 205 Indian soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice during the World Wars. As part of the professional engagements, personnel undertook cross-deck visits and exchanged operational experiences. The ship's crew also visited French Navy vessels Charles de Gaulle, Forbin and La Fayette, gaining insights into carrier operations, aviation facilities and practices onboard the vessels. INS Trishul also hosted a cultural interaction onboard, attended by Vice Admiral (Retd) Laurent Isnard, Deputy Mayor of Toulon, French Navy officers and civil dignitaries. A friendly volleyball match between personnel of the two navies further fostered camaraderie. The sea phase of Exercise Varuna saw INS Trishul operate alongside French Navy units, including FDA Forbin, FLF La Fayette and SNA Suffren, as well as NH90 helicopters and Atlantique 2 maritime patrol aircraft. The exercise featured anti-submarine and anti-surface warfare drills, live-firing exercises and cross-deck helicopter landing serials, aimed at enhancing operational coordination, interoperability and synergy between the two navies. The Indian Navy's deployment across the Mediterranean, Atlantic and adjoining maritime regions underscores its focus on operational readiness, maritime engagement and international outreach. The ongoing deployment and port call in Valencia are expected to further strengthen India's maritime engagement with partner navies and contribute to a secure and stable maritime environment, the Ministry of Defence said. The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) reviewed enforcement actions, inspections and compliance status across the National Capital Region (NCR) for the reporting period from September 8 to September 24, with 197 inspections conducted during the 17-day period, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change said on Friday. The 140th meeting of the Enforcement Task Force (ETF) of CAQM was held on October 1 to review the enforcement status. During the 17-day reporting period, a total of 197 inspections were reported, comprising 10 inspections at Construction & Demolition (C&D) sites, 111 inspections in the Industrial Sector and 76 inspections related to Diesel Generator (DG) sets. The industrial sector inspections included 22 inspections conducted as part of a special inspection drive. Based on the inspections, violations were reported in 85 cases, comprising 8 C&D cases, 49 industrial cases and 28 DG-related cases. As per the violations reported by the concerned sectors, various enforcement actions have been proposed. These include closure of 4 C&D projects and 1 industrial unit; sealing of 28 DG sets; issuance of orders/directions for compliance in 17 cases, including 4 DG sets; and Environmental Compensation (EC) in 10 cases. Other proposed actions include issuance of letters to project proponents, re-inspection, forwarding of cases to CPCB/SPCB, advisories and other appropriate follow-up measures. The ETF was apprised of the action taken during the special inspection drive conducted in Hapur, Uttar Pradesh on September 15 by 7 teams of the Flying Squads of the Commission, along with District Administration and Police personnel and officers of UPPCB. A total of 22 premises were inspected, of which 05 were found compliant and 1 had already been sealed by UPPCB. The actions suggested in the remaining cases include closure of 4 units, sealing of 1 DG set, issuance of orders in 5 cases, imposition of EC in 4 cases, and re-inspection and prosecution in 2 cases, the Ministry said. The status of resumption orders issued after the previous ETF meeting was also reviewed. As of September 30, a total of 9 resumption orders had been issued, comprising 2 industrial units and 7 C&D sites. State-wise, 1 resumption order was issued in Delhi, 3 in Haryana and 5 in Uttar Pradesh. Further, 1 case was transferred to the concerned State Pollution Control Board for...

national_raw_news.title: Demise of Dr Engam Pame, Nampibou Marinmai, H Lianvela PIB, CBC express deep grief ...
national_raw_news.content: Demise of Dr Engam Pame, Nampibou Marinmai, H Lianvela PIB, CBC express deep grief over tragic deaths - The Sangai Express - Largest Circulated NewsPaper in Manipur Demise of Dr Engam Pame, Nampibou Marinmai, H Lianvela PIB, CBC express deep grief over tragic deaths 02-Oct-2026 | IMPHAL, Oct 2 (PIB) The Press Information Bureau (PIB) and Central Bureau of Communication (CBC), Imphal, have expressed profound grief over the tragic demise of Dr Engam Pame, Additional Director General, PIB & CBC Regional Office, Imphal; Nampibou Marinmai, Director (News), DDK and All India Radio (AIR), Aizawl, and H Lianvela, Multi-Tasking Staff member, CBC, Aizawl, who lost their lives in a tragic road accident near Sateek in Mizoram on Thursday. Dr Engam Pame was a senior Indian Information Service (IIS) officer serving as Additional Director General, PIB & CBC Regional Office, Imphal. He joined the PIB/CBC Regional Office, Imphal, on July 29, 2022, as Regional Director. During his distinguished career, he had also served as Director, Directorate of Field Publicity, Shillong, and had been associated with the Regional News Unit of Doordarshan Kendra, Imphal. He was the Chairman of the Inter Media Publicity Coordination Committee (IMPCC), Manipur Chapter, it said. Born on November 30, 1967, Dr Pame made significant contributions to public communication and information dissemination, it added. During his tenure at PIB and CBC, Imphal, he played an important role in strengthening coordination between the Government and the media fraternity and in facilitating the dissemination of information on government Golicies, programmes and initiatives, it said. The statement continued that Nampibou Marinmai was also an IIS officer and was serving as Director (News), DDK and AIR, Aizawl. He was Chairman of the Inter Media Publicity Coordination Committee (IMPCC) and had earlier served as Public Relations Officer with the Ministry of Defence, Government of India. During his tenure with the Ministry of Defence, he was associated with defence-related public relations, media reporting and communication. Through his long association with news and public broadcasting, the PIB said that Marinmai made valuable contributions to public communication and information dissemination. Union Minister for Information and Broadcasting Ashwini Vaishnaw expressed deep sorrow over the demise of Dr Engam Pame, Nampibou Marinmai and H Lianvela and conveyed his heartfelt condolences to their bereaved families, friends and colleagues. Several senior officials of the Ministry and its attached organisations also expressed deep sorrow over the tragic loss and conveyed their heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families. They expressed solidarity with the families, friends and colleagues of the departed during this hour of immense grief. The Ministry of Defence also mourned the demise of Nampibou Marinmai, recalling his services as Public Relations Officer (Defence) and his long-standing association with defence reporting. Officials and staff of PIB, CBC and Akashvani, Imphal, observed a two-minute silence in memory of the departed souls and expressed their deepest condolences to the bereaved families. They also prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured driver and extended their support and solidarity to those affected by the tragedy....
